run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The only workload failing in the astronomy-shop namespace at the end of the authorized window is cart. Pod cart-74587775fc-9hbjm (node sregym-worker3) is in CrashLoopBackOff with 4 restarts and last termination reason Error / exit code 139 (last crash 02:10:17), and its container log shows 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' thrown from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected/Initialize at 02:08:25.8 and 02:08:26.6. The pod immediately before it, cart-74587775fc-k6swk on node sregym-worker, had connected to Redis successfully at 02:07:39 and served AddItem/GetCart until 02:08:11, then was stopped at 02:08:18 and replaced by the same ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc with an unchanged pod template. Because no cart container becomes ready, the cart Service (ClusterIP 10.96.209.202:8080) has no endpoint addresses, the cart Deployment reports Available=False / MinimumReplicasUnavailable (1 unavailable), and callers fail: the frontend logs repeated 'grpc 14 UNAVAILABLE ... connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.209.202:8080' and returns HTTP 500 on GET/POST /api/cart, while frontend-proxy and load-generator record HTTP 500/504 on those cart flows. Checked and healthy: valkey-cart pod (Running/Ready, 0 restarts, on sregym-worker, IP 10.244.234.161 present as a service endpoint, log 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 02:07:34, no restart or error), all 22 other astronomy-shop Deployments available/ready, all four Nodes Ready with no Memory/Disk/PID pressure, no NetworkPolicy and no ResourceQuota objects, and all flagd feature flags (incl. cartFailure, failedReadinessProbe) at defaultVariant 'off', so no flag-driven fault is switched on. The Deployment objects cart and valkey-cart were both created by helm at 02:07:32 with generation 1 and no later spec edit, so no configuration change to either workload was observed. Why the replacement cart pod could not open its Redis connection (its own init container did reach valkey-cart on 10.96.150.196:6379 at 02:08:19.6) and why the pod was replaced at all remain unresolved, and a separate client-side timeout from the same worker3 node (frontend -> product-catalog ClusterIP 10.96.141.151:8080, ETIMEDOUT recorded 02:09:56, while recommendation -> product-catalog succeeded from worker3 around 02:08:19) is recorded as an additional open hypothesis rather than as confirmed impact.

claims.text: Pod cart-74587775fc-9hbjm on node sregym-worker3 is not ready and is in CrashLoopBackOff: 4 restarts, waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 1m20s'), last termination reason Error with exitCode 139 at 2026-11-24T02:10:17Z.

The cart container logs 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' with the stack through cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() and ValkeyCartStore.Initialize() at 02:08:25.82Z (instance 0) and 02:08:26.65Z (instance 1) on pod cart-74587775fc-9hbjm.

The previous cart pod cart-74587775fc-k6swk on node sregym-worker logged 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 02:07:39.86Z, served GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync/EmptyCartAsync requests until 02:08:11Z, and was stopped at 02:08:18Z while ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc created the replacement pod cart-74587775fc-9hbjm at 02:08:18Z; the pod template hash (74587775fc) is unchanged between the two pods.

The cart Service (selector opentelemetry.io/name=cart, ClusterIP 10.96.209.202, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080) has no endpoint addresses ('<none>') while every other astronomy-shop Service in the same endpoints listing has at least one address.

Deployment cart reports Available=False (reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, lastUpdateTime 02:10:17Z) with 1 unavailable replica and no ready replicas, while all other 22 astronomy-shop Deployments report available=1/ready=1, including valkey-cart.

frontend pod frontend-6859c775df-bvrgc (node sregym-worker3) logged repeated 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.209.202:8080' between 02:08:27.98Z and 02:08:38.25Z, i.e. against the cart Service address.

frontend spans for GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart and the internal route 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' carry error=true, http.status_code=500, otel.status_code=ERROR with child client spans oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and /AddItem failing with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and grpc.error_message 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.209.202:8080'.

frontend-proxy spans 'GET' and 'POST' and load-generator spans 'GET' and 'POST' show error=true with http.status_code 500 and 504 (15 s proxy timeout) on the cart request paths inside the same trace set.

valkey-cart-859985f49d-dxjqf is Running and Ready with 0 restarts on node sregym-worker, pod IP 10.244.234.161 (present in the valkey-cart endpoints), and its log shows 'Valkey version=9.0.1 ... Running mode=standalone, port=6379' and 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 02:07:34.7Z with no error lines in the window; its deployment reports available=1/ready=1.

No network or quota object explains a refused connection: the NetworkPolicy query returned zero objects cluster-wide, the ResourceQuota query returned zero objects, and all four Nodes (sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3) are Ready with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure=False.

Injected feature-flag fault: rejected. The flagd ConfigMap demo.flagd.json has every flag at defaultVariant 'off' (including cartFailure, failedReadinessProbe, productCatalogFailure, paymentFailure, imageSlowLoad), and the cart crash stack is in ValkeyCartStore.Initialize, not in a flag-gated code path.

Configuration change to the cart or valkey workload: rejected as far as observable. Both Deployments cart and valkey-cart were created at 02:07:32Z by manager helm (operation Apply), are at generation 1, and carry no later spec-writing manager entry, so no post-deployment spec edit to either object was recorded.

The cart crash loop is caused by a broken Redis connection path for the new cart pod on sregym-worker3 rather than by the cart image or template: the same template on sregym-worker connected to valkey-cart successfully at 02:07:39, the new pod's own wait-for-valkey-cart init container reached valkey-cart (10.96.150.196:6379) at 02:08:19.6, and the cart container then failed in EnsureRedisConnected seconds later. NetworkPolicy, ResourceQuota, node pressure and flagd are excluded, so the remaining candidate is a connectivity or acceptance fault between that pod and valkey-cart that the available sources cannot pinpoint.

A second, separate new-connection problem may affect pods on sregym-worker3: frontend (worker3) oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct calls to ClusterIP 10.96.141.151:8080 failed with 'connect ETIMEDOUT' (error recorded 02:09:56Z, after the authorized window end), while recommendation, also on worker3, completed oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts against the same service at 02:08:19.07Z in 3.3 ms and product-catalog's own server span took 1.36 ms; product-catalog server spans show rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

Recommendation: restore the cart workload first - verify from sregym-worker3 that a pod can open a TCP connection to valkey-cart:6379 (for example delete the CrashLoopBackOff pod so it can be rescheduled onto another node) and re-check valkey-cart's acceptance of new connections (maxclients, listen backlog) while watching whether frontend product-catalog connect timeouts from worker3 continue.

gaps: The reason the replacement cart pod could not establish its Redis connection is not established: the cart client log prints only the outer "Wasn't able to connect to redis" message and the inner StackExchange.Redis exception text was not found in the pod's logs inside the window.

The trigger for the pod replacement at 02:08:18 (ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc created cart-74587775fc-9hbjm and the previous pod cart-74587775fc-k6swk was stopped) is unknown; no object-level change to the cart Deployment (generation 1, helm Apply at 02:07:32) or its ReplicaSet template was observed, and change history is not integrated in this Run.

Calico-specific objects that could hold an injected connectivity policy (networkpolicies.crd.projectcalico.org, globalnetworkpolicies.crd.projectcalico.org, adminnetworkpolicies.policy.networking.k8s.io, networksets.crd.projectcalico.org) exist as CRDs but cannot be read with the available Kubernetes query kinds, so a Calico-level fault can be neither confirmed nor excluded.

Direct inspection of the Valkey server state was not possible: the configured Redis/Valkey credential was refused by the server (REDIS_AUTH_FAILED), so client counts, maxclients and memory/persistence state of valkey-cart could not be verified; that tool error is a source limitation, not evidence about the workload.

The frontend -> product-catalog 'connect ETIMEDOUT 10.96.141.151:8080' failure is recorded at 02:09:56Z, after the authorized window end (02:08:40Z), so whether product-catalog connectivity was degraded during the window itself is unknown; only successful product-catalog spans at 02:08:19 were observed.

Prometheus queries for traces_span_metrics_calls_total and for container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds_total / container_cpu_usage_seconds_total over cart pods returned no samples in the queried windows (01:58-02:08:40 and 02:03:40-02:08:40), and container_memory_working_set_bytes for cart-74587775fc-9hbjm returned no samples, so span-metric error rates and cart container CPU-throttling/memory readings around the incident could not be used; the findings above rest on Jaeger traces, Loki logs and the Kubernetes API instead.

The kube-state-metrics pod list at 02:08:43 did not include a load-generator pod although Prometheus carries series for load-generator-69fcd4cb96-s2lt8 and load-generator spans appear at 02:08:19-02:09:56, so the load-generator's own pod status was not verified.
next_steps: From a privileged shell, test TCP reachability from a pod scheduled on sregym-worker3 to 10.244.234.161:6379 and compare with a pod on sregym-worker to confirm or refute a node-local new-connection problem.
Inspect valkey-cart server-side state (INFO clients, maxclients, connected_clients, listen backlog) with credentials the server accepts.
Check Calico network policy objects and felix logs for sregym-worker3 around 02:08:18-02:08:26, which are not readable with the current tool set.
Confirm whether the cart pod stop at 02:08:18 was an operator or controller action by inspecting the audit log or change history, which is not integrated in this Run.

view.cannot_prove: A line that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only limit lines are shown (the newest), and retention, ingest delay, the label selector and line filters can leave gaps. The timestamp is when the line was ingested or parsed, not necessarily when the event happened. A metric query counts only lines inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
